knowledge-base.name: lang-r
knowledge-base.triggers: R, .R, .Rmd, .qmd, .Rproj, DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, renv.lock, tidyverse, dplyr, ggplot2, purrr, testthat, devtools, roxygen2, renv, RStudio, Quarto, R Markdown, Shiny
knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for R. Loaded automatically when agents work on .R, .Rmd, .qmd, DESCRIPTION, or NAMESPACE files. Applies to R 4.1+, statistical computing, data analysis, R packages, and Shiny apps.

core-principles.principle: Use tidyverse conventions for data manipulation, visualization, and functional programming; fall back to base R only when performance demands it.
Prefer vectorized operations and purrr::map() over explicit for loops; R is optimized for vector operations.
Every analysis must be reproducible — use renv for dependency management, set.seed() for stochastic operations, and R Markdown/Quarto for literate programming.
Write pure functions with no side effects; avoid modifying global state or relying on .GlobalEnv.
No reliance on partial matching, implicit type coercion, or positional argument passing for non-trivial functions.

guardrail.rule: Never use require() in scripts or packages. Use library() at the top of scripts; use DESCRIPTION Imports: in packages.
guardrail.bad: require(dplyr) # silently returns FALSE if missing
guardrail.good: library(dplyr) # errors loudly if package is missing

guardrail.rule: Never use T/F as TRUE/FALSE aliases. They can be overwritten: T <- FALSE is valid R.
Never use attach() or setwd(). Use here::here() for project-relative paths.
Never use try(). Always use tryCatch() or purrr::safely() for recoverable error handling.
Use <- for assignment. Never use = for assignment at top level (only inside function arguments).
Always use set.seed() before stochastic operations; document the seed value.
Run styler::style_pkg() and lintr::lint_package() before every commit.
Use rlang::abort() or cli::cli_abort() over stop() for structured conditions with machine-readable classes.
Use vapply() over sapply() when base R is required (explicit return type guarantees type safety).
guardrail.bad: sapply(x, nchar) # return type not guaranteed
guardrail.good: vapply(x, nchar, integer(1)) # always returns integer vector

guardrail.rule: Reserve for loops for side effects only (writing files, API calls). Use vectorized functions or purrr::map() for transformations.

version-dependencies.item: Manage dependencies with renv — always commit renv.lock
For packages, declare all dependencies in DESCRIPTION (Imports:, Suggests:)
Pin CRAN snapshot dates in renv for full reproducibility
Audit new dependencies: check CRAN status, reverse dependencies, license (GPL compatibility)

code-style.item: Run styler::style_pkg() and lintr::lint_package() before every commit
Naming: snake_case for functions/variables, PascalCase for R6/S4 classes
Use <- for assignment (not = outside function arguments)
Explicit library() at top of scripts; never use require()
Always use TRUE/FALSE (never T/F — they can be overwritten)
No attach() or setwd() — use here::here() for project-relative paths

vectorization.item: Prefer vectorized operations: x * 2 not for (i in seq_along(x)) x[i] * 2
Use dplyr::mutate() / dplyr::summarise() for column-wise transformations
Use purrr::map() family for list iteration (map_dbl(), map_chr(), map_dfr())
Use dplyr::across() for applying functions to multiple columns
Reserve for loops for side effects only (writing files, API calls)
Use vapply() over sapply() when base R is required (explicit return type)

directory.purpose: Scripts that produce data objects in data/
Exported/imported symbols (never edit manually; roxygen2 generates this)

project-structure.note: Use roxygen2 for all docs; never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand. Raw data is immutable.

pattern.name: Tidyverse Pipe Chains
pattern.example: result <- raw_data |> dplyr::filter(year >= 2020, !is.na(revenue)) |> dplyr::mutate( revenue_m = revenue / 1e6, growth = (revenue - dplyr::lag(revenue)) / dplyr::lag(revenue) ) |> dplyr::summarise( mean_revenue = mean(revenue_m, na.rm = TRUE), .by = region )

pattern.name: Tidy Evaluation
pattern.description: Use {{ }} (embrace) for column names passed as arguments, .data pronoun for string references, across() for multiple columns.

pattern.name: ggplot2 Grammar of Graphics
Functional Programming with purrr
pattern.example:
# Type-stable map variants -- read and combine CSV files results <- purrr::map_dfr(file_paths, \(path) { readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) |> dplyr::mutate(source_file = basename(path)) })
# Safe execution -- capture errors without stopping safe_read <- purrr::safely(readr::read_csv) reads <- purrr::map(file_paths, safe_read) successes <- purrr::map(purrr::keep(reads, \(x) is.null(x$error)), "result")

pattern.name: Input Validation with cli

testing.coverage-target: 80% for business logic, 60% overall (measured with covr)

setup.item: Test files: test-*.R (mirror source: data-clean.R -> test-data-clean.R)
Use snapshot tests (expect_snapshot()) for complex output (plots, printed tables)
No test interdependencies — each test_that() block is self-contained
Use withr::local_*() for temporary state changes (env vars, options, files)

quick-reference.item: here::here() always; never setwd() or absolute paths
renv for lockfile; renv.lock committed; DESCRIPTION for packages
|> pipes + dplyr/purrr; for loops for side effects only
rlang::abort() or cli::cli_abort(); tryCatch() not try()
{{ }} for column args; .data[[ ]] for string column names
testthat 3e; expect_snapshot() for complex output; withr for state
roxygen2 for packages; never edit man/ or NAMESPACE manually
set.seed() before stochastic ops; session_info() at end of reports
